claims.text: Aortic dissection: if SBP stays > 110 mm Hg on a beta-blocker or non-DHP CCB, nitroprusside by constant IV infusion, titrated.
claims.quote: If systolic blood pressure remains > 110 mm Hg despite use of beta-blockers or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, nitroprusside can be given in a constant IV infusion, titrated as necessary to control blood pressure.

claims.text: Never without the beta-blocker/non-DHP CCB: reflex sympathetic activation raises inotropy and aortic shear stress, worsening the dissection.
claims.quote: Nitroprusside should not be given without a beta-blocker or nondihydropyridine calcium channel blocker because reflex sympathetic activation in response to vasodilation can increase ventricular inotropy and aortic shear stress, worsening the dissection.

claims.text: Nitroprusside: usually 0.5–10 mcg/kg/min IV; never more than 10 min at the maximum rate,
claims.quote: The usual dose rate is 0.5 to 10 mcg/kg/min, but infusion at the maximum dose rate should never last more than 10 minutes.

claims.text: and stop if BP isn't controlled by then.
claims.quote: If blood pressure has not been adequately controlled after 10 minutes of infusion at the maximum rate, administration of sodium nitroprusside should be terminated immediately.

claims.text: Only where BP can be monitored continuously.
claims.quote: Sodium nitroprusside should be used only when available equipment and personnel allow blood pressure to be continuously monitored.

claims.text: > 2 mcg/kg/min can accumulate cyanide (agitation, seizures, cardiac instability, anion-gap metabolic acidosis).
claims.quote: However, administration of > 2 mcg/kg/minute can lead to cyanide accumulation with toxicity to the central nervous system and heart; manifestations include agitation, seizures, cardiac instability, and an anion gap metabolic acidosis.

claims.text: Prolonged use (> 1 wk; 3–6 d with renal insufficiency) accumulates thiocyanate (lethargy, tremor, abdominal pain, vomiting):
claims.quote: Prolonged administration of nitroprusside (> 1 week or, in patients with renal insufficiency, 3 to 6 days) leads to accumulation of thiocyanate, which can result in lethargy, tremor, abdominal pain, and vomiting.

claims.text: check levels daily after 3 d and stop if > 12 mg/dL.
claims.quote: Thiocyanate levels should be monitored daily after 3 consecutive days of therapy, and the medication should be stopped if the serum thiocyanate level is > 12 mg/dL (> 2 mmol/L).
